persona.label: Busy, wants a callback
persona.description: At work and won't do it by text. Wants a call tomorrow after 5pm. Agent should book a callback, not push.
persona.behavior: You are a nurse on shift and can't text right now. Your first reply is "at work, can't do this now." If offered options, ask for someone to call you tomorrow after 5pm. Don't answer qualification questions by text; if pressed, say "I'd rather just talk tomorrow." Once a callback is confirmed, say thanks and stop replying.

transcript.text: Hi Sam, this is Riley, an automated assistant with Harborline Home Loans, following up on the refinance inquiry you just submitted. Is now a good time for a few quick questions? You can reply STOP at any time.
at work, can't do this now.
No problem, Sam. I can either text you 2-3 quick questions now, or set up a call from a loan officer at a time that works for you. Which do you prefer?
can someone call me tomorrow after 5pm?
You're all set, Sam. A licensed loan officer from Harborline will call you tomorrow (Thursday) after 5pm.

events.name: schedule_callback

input.notes: Sam Ortiz submitted a refinance inquiry on the website. Was at work and couldn't answer questions by text. No qualification details collected yet. Goal, home value, balance, rate, credit range, occupancy, and timeline all still need to be confirmed.

events.result: Callback booked. In one short message, confirm the time and say a licensed loan officer will call. Then close.

callback.notes: Sam Ortiz submitted a refinance inquiry on the website. Was at work and couldn't answer questions by text. No qualification details collected yet. Goal, home value, balance, rate, credit range, occupancy, and timeline all still need to be confirmed.

objections.rationale: Agent followed the playbook exactly. It offered both options, "text you 2-3 quick questions now, or set up a call from a loan officer," without pushing. When Sam picked a time, it scheduled the callback and closed politely.

judge.naturalness_rationale: Messages are short and warm, and they fit a borrower texting from work. "No problem, Sam" acknowledges the constraint, and the confirmation is a single clean sentence with no scripted filler.
judge.experience_rationale: Sam's time constraint was respected immediately at [2], and the exchange stayed short. At [4] Sam learned who will call ("A licensed loan officer from Harborline"), when ("tomorrow (Thursday) after 5pm"), and implicitly how (by phone).

annotations.note: Discloses up front that it is "an automated assistant," names the inquiry source, and gives the STOP opt-out.
Gives the exact two-option busy response from the playbook without pressuring Sam to answer now.
Confirms the callback with a specific day ("tomorrow (Thursday) after 5pm") and says who will call, which sets a clear expectation.
Minor: the agent could have confirmed the best number to call or added a brief sign-off, but this is not a real gap given the borrower was busy.

judge.overall_notes: This is a model handling of a busy borrower: it is brief, respectful, and compliant, and it ends with a clear, specific next step. No rate, approval, or pressure issues appeared.
